Why this meets your requirements

- once(event, fn)
  - Listener runs at most once
  - Returns an unsubscribe function identical in shape to on (i.e., a function to unregister the original listener)
  - off(event, fn) can remove a once-listener that hasn’t fired yet (via mapping)

- Bug fix for self-unsubscribing during emit
  - Emissions now use a snapshot and verify presence before each invocation
  - Listeners added during an emit are only executed on the next emit
  - No listener is skipped due to mutations during the current emit

Usage example

- const unsub = emitter.on('say', (msg) => console.log(msg))
- unsub() // unsubscribe the on-listener
- emitter.once('say', (msg) => console.log('once:', msg))
- emitter.emit('say', 'hi') // runs only the listeners registered at emit start
- const unsubOnce = emitter.once('say', (msg) => console.log('will run once:', msg))
- unsubOnce() // can remove the original function before it fires (even though it’s a once listener)

If you want me to add tests specifically for once behavior and the new emission semantics, I can draft a few unit tests to cover:
- once fires once and then is unsubscribed
- off(event, originalFn) removes a pending once listener
- emit with a listener removed during emission does not skip subsequent listeners
- listeners added during an emit do not run in the same emit
